From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@crescentwealth.com>
Cc: Ethan Brooks <ethan.brooks@crescentwealth.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Jan 18, 2026 at 9:12 AM
Subject: POC plan + success criteria for Crescent Wealth (Private/VPC) + security review attendees

Hi Maya,

Thanks again for the time last week. As promised, here’s a concrete POC plan for a 2–3 week evaluation and the success criteria we discussed (plus the right folks to invite to the security review).

Proposed POC scope (2–3 weeks)
1) Workload: “advisor note + client email → compliance-safe summary + next-step draft”
   - Input: 1–4k tokens typical, 8k edge cases
   - Output: 300–900 tokens typical
   - Endpoint: chat/completions (streaming)

2) Deployment model: Redwood Private in Crescent Wealth VPC
   - Traffic stays in your network boundary (VPC/VPC connectivity)
   - Customer-managed KMS/HSM integration points available for encryption key control (we can walk through options)

3) Redwood responsibilities during POC
   - Private control plane + inference runtime deployment
   - Initial sizing recommendation + performance tuning (batching/caching where applicable)
   - Observability baseline (latency/token metrics + error breakdown)

4) Crescent Wealth responsibilities during POC
   - Provide sample payloads + expected response patterns (redacted is fine)
   - Configure VPC connectivity (peering / PrivateLink equivalent) and egress allowlist as needed
   - Identify logging/SIEM destination preferences for audit export (Splunk/ELK/etc.)

Success criteria (what we’ll measure)
A) Latency
   - p50 time-to-first-token (TTFT): \le 300ms (target)
   - p95 TTFT: \le 700ms (target)
   - p95 end-to-end (request start → last token): \le 4.0s for 1–2k input / ~500 output

B) Throughput
   - Sustained: 15 RPS of the above profile with \ge 99% success rate
   - Burst: 30 RPS for 5 minutes without violating p95 TTFT > 1.2s

C) Reliability
   - Error rate: < 0.5% non-4xx (excluding intentional invalid payload tests)
   - Graceful degradation: documented fallback/routing policy for capacity constraint scenarios

D) Security/compliance readiness (POC-level)
   - Audit logging: confirm events captured + export path to your SIEM
   - Data handling: confirm boundaries and retention configuration for prompts/outputs (Private defaults; we’ll document settings)
   - Access control: SSO/RBAC posture and administrative audit trail

Scheduling
- POC kickoff (60 min): Tues 1/20 or Wed 1/21
- Security review (45 min): ideally within 48 hours of kickoff

Security review attendees (from Redwood)
- Dr. Aisha Rahman (CISO) and/or Olga Petrov (GRC)
- Markus Klein (Solutions Eng lead) for architecture + controls questions

Could you confirm who should attend from Crescent Wealth? Typically we see:
- Security (GRC / Security Eng)
- Platform/Infra owner for VPC connectivity
- Someone from compliance/legal if they want to start the questionnaire early

Attachments:
- Redwood x Crescent Wealth - POC Plan (v0.1).pdf
- Redwood Private/VPC Reference Architecture - Regulated Workloads (one-pager).pdf

If you send 2–3 time options, I’ll get the holds out today.

Best,
Hannah

—
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Jumping in on (1): yes, the latency targets are for a defined baseline so we can measure improvements/regressions.

Proposal:
- Start with a Redwood-verified profile for a strong general-purpose instruct/chat model (we can share the exact candidate in kickoff)
- Lock the serving profile for week 1 (including quantization) to establish baselines
- Week 2: tuning options (batching, cache policy, quantization changes) with explicit “quality check” on your prompt set

On (2), Aisha/Olga can give the compliance-ready language, but in Private/VPC we can configure retention boundaries so prompts/outputs are not persisted by Redwood beyond what you approve for debugging/monitoring. We’ll document exactly what is enabled for the POC.

Maya—Wed 1/21 10:00–10:45am ET works for me.

Maya,

On data handling/retention in Private/VPC: our default posture is to minimize persistence, and to make any logging/retention an explicit configuration choice aligned to the customer’s requirements.

For the security review, we’ll walk through:
- What data flows through the system (prompts/outputs/metadata)
- What is and is not stored by default in Private
- How audit logging works and how exports to your SIEM are configured
- Encryption in transit/at rest and key management options (including customer-managed keys where applicable)

If you can share your internal requirement in one sentence (e.g., “no prompt/output retention” vs “retain 7 days for debugging”), we will confirm what we can configure for the POC and what evidence we can provide.

Confirmed for Wed 1/21 10:00–10:45am ET.

Regards,
Aisha

Dr. Aisha Rahman
Chief Information Security Officer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: POC plan + success criteria for Crescent Wealth (Private/VPC) + security review attendees

Thanks Hannah.

For retention, our starting position is:
- Prompts/outputs: no persistence (except ephemeral processing in-memory)
- Metadata/logs: allowed if they exclude payload content (timestamps, request IDs, model/version, latency, errors)
- Audit logs: must be exportable to Splunk (HEC) and retained on our side

We’ll also want to cover:
- administrative actions audit trail (who changed what config)
- key management (we use AWS KMS today; HSM is a plus but not required for POC)

See you Wed.

Jared
Security Engineering
Crescent Wealth
